fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Everyone Is a Musical Genius", "body": "ShaOne opens with the epiphany that arrived while he was building his slides: everyone is an inherent musical genius, because anyone who has ever responded to music emotionally or imaginatively is already using the gift. He calls his approach imaginal listening, boiled down to listen, feel and imagine, and traces it to his own childhood, gigging within about six months of picking up music at around eleven. Chance frames the show itself around a similar belief, that every person carries some realization no one else alive has had, while ShaOne credits years of cold computer code as the Saturnian teacher that balanced music's warm flow."}, {"title": "Socrates and the Art You Skipped", "body": "Gabe maps the conversation onto Plato's Symposium, where seven speakers pass a touchstone around the room, which he likens to the podium, the altar and even the mute button on a live call. Socrates sits in the seventh seat, and Gabe reads his name backwards as Set Arcos, the Archon of Set. In prison before the hemlock, Socrates hears his daimonic spirit say he never figured out music, so he spends his last hours writing dithyrambs. Gabe's lesson is that a plateau is an invitation to find the art you neglected and begin again as a child, and he adds that music minus use leaves the mic."}, {"title": "One String, Twelve Tones", "body": "ShaOne calls music the language of the monad, and the monad's other name, the monochord, leads him to the Pythagorean single string as the root of all music theory. Touch a string lightly at its halfway point and it sounds an octave higher, so the harmonics are discovered rather than invented. Inspired by Santos Bonacci's sine wave of the zodiac, ShaOne lays the 12 chromatic tones on a 12 phase wheel, treats the 13th as the spiral into the next octave, and shows each of the seven modes as its own pattern of tones and semitones, which Gabe hears as Set Arcos once more."}, {"title": "The Ionian: Home in the Sun", "body": "ShaOne presents the Ionian, the ordinary major scale, as home base: resolved, friendly and free of dissonance, the stuff of melodies children sing at school. Its planet is the sun and its metal gold, with Aries as the main sign and Aquarius as a secondary pull toward adventure, like leaving the Shire, and the group lights up when Aries turns out to be an anagram of shire. Gabe brings in the Sun tarot card, number 19, which reduces to one. Chance tastes the mode as a sweet orange in warm sunlight and ties it to the sacral chakra, while ShaOne sees a golden sun at the crown."}, {"title": "Dorian, Mood and Doom", "body": "ShaOne plays the Dorian as a minor scale with a raised sixth, the bluesy, Pink Floyd flavored lightest of the dark modes, like Venus appearing before nightfall. He notes that mode is mood, and the group reads mood backwards as doom in its older sense of fate or judgment. Gabe overlays his Enneagram, crossing from one to two over the River Styx as Achilles faces Agamemnon, and hears D Orion in the name. Chance pictures a pine tree, Gabe recounts the 1755 Lisbon disaster and Voltaire's poem ending on hope, and a Hazrat Inayat Khan passage on becoming musical in thought closes part one."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Sean Clark (sha0ne), UK musician and lifelong improviser, maps the seven musical modes onto planets, alchemical metals, zodiac signs, and the enneagram, with live guitar demonstrations, and makes the case that imaginal listening is innate to every human being.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: Covers the seven musical modes as occult keys to emotion, planets, and zodiac, imaginal listening as the practice of connecting genius to sound, the Socrates daemon music story, the mode-mood-doom etymological thread, Santos Bonacci's sine wave zodiac mapped onto the 12 chromatic tones, Ionian as solar/Aries home base, Dorian as the lunar/Scorpionic gateway to mystery, the Slick Dissident enneagram overlay on the modal system, and a palindrome discovery in the Dorian mode teased for part two.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Harmony Is the Answer to Life", "body": "Opening the extension before Gabe rejoins, Chance thanks ShaOne for approaching music with curiosity instead of the mind control paranoia that usually dominates the topic in their circles. ShaOne answers that music trained him back into childlike appreciation, and borrows a Buddhist teaching about containers: a powerful fire needs a strong hearth. Chance shares his own resolution of the biggest question, that the meaning of life is life itself and that harmony is how existence keeps going. ShaOne recalls watching the needle on a vinyl record as the living now, with the rest of the music already waiting in the groove."}, {"title": "The Phrygian and the Art of Holding Tension", "body": "ShaOne introduces the Phrygian as the point where things get very spicy, its magic note sitting a single semitone above the root, a sound metal bands love. Gabe sees desert camels and the three wise men, reading their gold, frankincense and myrrh as land, air and water. Chance ties the mode's Libra association to Anatolia as the gate to the underworld and hears Mars in Libra as hot, dry and passive aggressive. The mode becomes a portrait of a warrior's power to sustain tension, and the conversation settles on a mirage, a resolution that always feels one step away."}, {"title": "Lydian Desire and the Craft of Denial", "body": "ShaOne calls the Lydian his favorite mode, a major scale with a raised fourth that feels like a home in the clouds. Chance places it at the crown chakra and retells the myth of Tantalus, arguing the mode is tantalizing rather than tense, a hunger for another bite because it is delicious. Gabe maps it to the Enneagram seven, the enthusiast whose shadow is gluttony, and reframes that type as an epicure who wants only the finest things. Denial turns up hidden inside the word Lydian, and Chance later extends it: a scale is defined less by its notes than by which steps it denies."}, {"title": "Aeolian Sorrow and the Party Built on Tragedy", "body": "ShaOne plays the Aeolian as the classic sad mode, traditionally linked to Saturn, and insists there is something really beautiful in minor keys and heavier moods. Chance assigns it to the heart chakra, the seat of a heavy heart. Gabe continues his Symposium mapping: Alcibiades dances up to Agathon, the tragedian hosting the night, whose muse Melpomene twirls a dagger and holds a frowning mask, so the whole party exists because of a tragedy. The visions it stirs range from floating in a choppy, foggy sea to Gabe's melting snow and dripping icicles, the weather itself crying."}, {"title": "Mirrors, a Palindrome, and the Dorian Door", "body": "Reaching the Locrian, the most unstable mode, ShaOne says it sounds like all the wrong notes and has to keep moving to stay musical, and Chance ties that restlessness to the root chakra and the survival grind of a job with nowhere to rest. ShaOne then reveals his discovery that the seven step patterns hold one palindrome and three exact mirrors. The pairs line up by feeling: Ionian home against Phrygian battle, Lydian heights against Locrian depths, Mixolydian party against Aeolian isolation. ShaOne arranges them as a menorah with the Dorian palindrome at the center, a door he now wants to play from."}]

Find the art that you didn't gain mastery over and start over as a child again.", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "This astrology thing is music, but it's presented as geometry and mythology pointing to the energy forms.", "author": "ShaOne", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/90a31d85-3123-4197-a3f7-9a20ca2fc505/SHA0NE.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I'm constantly seeing beautiful examples of how harmonious it is to consider the opposite to also have validity.", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Conjecture's wonderful. I love it, but it needs the solid basis, and then it can just launch off.", "author": "ShaOne", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/90a31d85-3123-4197-a3f7-9a20ca2fc505/SHA0NE.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The sacral chakra in a coherent state, it carries the signatures of satisfaction and pleasure and also creativity and flow.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "There's something satisfying about musical resolution which is physical. It's emotional, sure, it's conceptual, but it's just the body's like, \"Oh, yeah.\"", "author": "ShaOne", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/90a31d85-3123-4197-a3f7-9a20ca2fc505/SHA0NE.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The systems, the powers that be, they have learned how to capitalize on disaster.", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "There's something called the smell of zen, which a teacher of mine used to describe whenever you get a true, just boof, experience of how things truly are.", "author": "ShaOne", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/90a31d85-3123-4197-a3f7-9a20ca2fc505/SHA0NE.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}]
